Prepare listing content and remediation responses

approval.cost: No fee stated in the docs read
approval.trigger: Required before external users can add a public OR unlisted app: 'all public apps must undergo a dedicated App Submission Review process for app security, functionality and information'. Stages: submission completeness and branding; functionality, usability, and compliance review (Zoom installs/uninstalls your app and tests the data flow); security review (technical design review, OAuth scope evaluation for least privilege, and security testing against the OWASP Top 10 including scanning and manual misuse testing). Failures return as a report with action items for a remediation loop, and monitoring continues after publication (Zoom may demand remediation or remove the app). Internal and private apps (your own account only) skip the standard review.
approval.wait: Explicitly unpublished: 'an app's review time varies based on app quality, usability, quantity and function of features, and clarity of information'. The one stated response time is for beta sharing requests: no longer than 3-4 business days

blockers.detail: Adding a scope is literally 'submitting a request to the Zoom Security Review team', each scope needs a written justification at build time, and reviewers 'may reject the scope request' or tell you to remove scopes. Over-requesting is a rejection and remediation trigger.
blockers.howToClear: Request the minimal scope set with a concrete justification per scope; supply security evidence (SSDLC, SAST/DAST results, penetration test) proactively.
blockers.title: Scopes are reviewed, not just declared

blockers.detail: Unlisted status only hides you from Marketplace search; it 'does not avoid review'. Teams budgeting for a quiet unlisted launch still face the full security, functionality, and compliance process.
blockers.howToClear: Plan the review timeline (unpublished duration) into any external launch, listed or not.
blockers.title: Unlisted does not mean unreviewed

blockers.detail: Even after Zoom approves your app, a customer's Zoom account can require admin pre-approval before its users add apps; users file a request and the account admin/owner approves or declines in the Marketplace admin portal. Zoom's approval does not override customer admin policy.
blockers.howToClear: Ship admin-facing approval instructions and expect an admin step in enterprise onboarding.
blockers.title: Customer admin pre-approval is a second gate

flavor.recommended: A General app in the Zoom App Marketplace, user-managed
flavor.why: The General app is the user-level OAuth app: authorization code grant, each user consents ('Allow'), and you receive an access token plus refresh token for that user. At creation you also pick the management model (user-managed: individuals add/manage it themselves, Zoom's own example is a calendar integration; admin-managed: org admins control it) and the distribution type, which decides whether Marketplace review applies.

humanMust: Hold a Zoom account whose role has the 'Zoom for developers' permission (an admin enables it in Role Settings)
Make the management-model and distribution choices
Write scope justifications and the Technical Design section
Submit for review and work the remediation loop
name: Zoom
nuances: User OAuth access tokens last one hour (expires_in 3599 in Zoom's example), renewed with the refresh token. Server-to-Server tokens also last one hour with no refresh token, and multiple concurrently valid tokens per app are allowed.
Deauthorization is a build requirement: when a user removes a production app, Zoom POSTs an app_deauthorized event to your deauthorization endpoint, and 'apps must delete all associated user data'.

Changes to a published app's production configuration require an update request approved by the Marketplace team, and scope changes force users to reauthorize (per a Zoom Support statement; see evidence flags).

A public client with PKCE exists for backend-less clients (separate public client ID; may need a written PKCE justification for the review team). Enabling it turns on 'multi-auth token' mode; loopback redirect URIs are allowed only for PKCE/native clients, others must use HTTPS.
Private/beta apps can never be published to the Marketplace directly, and beta authorization URLs become invalid once the app is published.
prerequisites: A Zoom account with the 'Zoom for developers' role permission
Your OAuth redirect URL and allow list
A scope list with a written justification per scope
A Technical Design document (stack, architecture, data handling, security controls, scope use) and listing content

steps.detail: Zoom App Marketplace > Develop > Build App > General app > Create. Prerequisite: your account role must carry the 'Zoom for developers' permission (User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features).
steps.title: Create a General app

steps.detail: App name; management model (user-managed for self-serve user connection); app credentials (the build flow keeps separate Development and Production credential sets); OAuth information: redirect URL for OAuth plus an OAuth allow list.
steps.title: Complete Basic Info

steps.detail: Select the products/features the app works with (Meetings, in-client surfaces, etc.). On the Scopes page, add scopes per product and write a Scope Description justifying each one; treat every scope as a request the Security Review team can reject.
steps.title: Select products and scopes (with justifications)

steps.detail: Use 'Add App Now' to authorize the app on your own account and test the flow end to end; preview the Marketplace listing page.
steps.title: Local Test on your own account

steps.detail: Complete the app listing and the mandatory Technical Design section: technology stack, architecture, data handling, security controls, and how each OAuth scope is used. Weak metadata 'will fail app review'.
steps.title: Write the Technical Design and listing

steps.detail: Authorize at zoom.us/oauth/authorize (response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri); exchange the code at zoom.us/oauth/token; refresh with the refresh token. Also implement the deauthorization endpoint: Zoom POSTs app_deauthorized when a user removes a production app, and you must delete all associated user data.
steps.title: Implement the flow, including deauthorization

steps.detail: Submit for review. Expect the three stages (completeness/branding, functionality/compliance, security with scope evaluation and OWASP Top 10 testing), then remediation rounds from the report's action items. Review duration is explicitly variable and unpublished. After approval, customer admins may still pre-approve before their users can add the app.
steps.title: Submit for Marketplace review

tagline: A real security review stands between you and external users, listed or unlisted: every scope is individually justified and evaluated, your technical design is tested against the OWASP Top 10, and Zoom publishes no review duration at all.

time.active: ~1 day of build-flow configuration, justifications, and Technical Design writing, plus flow code and remediation cycles
time.total: External launch waits on a review whose duration Zoom does not publish
time.waiting: Review: unstated and explicitly variable; beta share requests answered within 3-4 business days (stated)
